trial_court: Judge, Family Court, Pauri Garhwal in Family Court Case No. 60 of 2018
case_name: Smt. Shakuntala Umrao vs Ram Sharan Umrao
facts_of_case: The parties got married on 05.02.2016. The wife filed for divorce under Section 13(1)(ia) and (ib) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 due to alleged cruelty by the husband. The trial court dismissed the suit.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove it by substantial evidence.
legal_principles.held: While arriving at this finding, the Judge, Family Court, Pauri Garhwal took into consideration the statements made by the appellant in her cross-examination, the statement made by Vishambar Dayal-PW-2 in his cross examination, and the statement made by Mayaram-PW-3 in his cross examination.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce on the ground of desertion must prove it by substantial evidence.
legal_principles.held: At present, the appellant has not been able to prove the fact of desertion being done by the respondent without any reason by substantial evidence.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must prove their case by substantial evidence.
legal_principles.held: In such a situation, on the basis of desertion under Section 13(1)(i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the relief of divorce cannot be granted to the appellant.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree dated 18.12.2021 passed by the Judge, Family Court, Pauri Garhwal in Family Court Case No. 60 of 2018 is set aside.
